propositions: Three independent sites in push.py, enrich_drain.py, and compact_trigger.py implement detached-child spawn with near-identical logic including PYTHONPATH bootstrap, detach flags, and cwd handling, creating maintenance burden and propagating defects identically across all three copies.

Bug 3198 (missing cwd in Popen) appeared at all three sites identically due to deliberate copy-paste imitation, demonstrating that defects replicate through duplicate spawn implementations rather than being caught once at a single source.

A fourth detached-spawn site (gc_trigger.py) landed concurrently with the consolidation effort, reproducing the same copy-paste pattern and proving the structural problem persists without enforcement.

The three sites differ materially in env construction (push.py uses secret-stripped projection plus REBAR_SYNC_PUSH; drain/sweep use plain os.environ) and exception handling (push.py catches OSError with %r logging; drain/sweep catch broad Exception with exc_info=True), requiring per-caller env/error logic while the spawn mechanism itself consolidates.
A static test must enforce that the detached-spawn signature (DETACHED_PROCESS/CREATE_NO_WINDOW tokens and sys.path.insert re-entry stub) appears only in _proc.py to prevent future copy-paste sites.
